target_outcomes.current_statement: Vehicles on public highways need a PMVI at least annually; ambulances require a check every six months, and a new vehicle's next inspection is due two years after its initial inspection when first sold.
When turn indicators stop working, communicate turns with hand signals until repairs are made.
Driving involves the surroundings, the vehicle and the driver. Only the driver gathers information, applies skill, knowledge, experience and judgment, and acts to complete the task safely.

Drive on the right half of the roadway, pass oncoming vehicles on the right, give opposite-direction traffic at least half of the main traveled roadway on narrow roads, and when moving slower than other traffic you should use the extreme right lane.

Passing on the right is permitted when the vehicle ahead is about to turn left without driving off the pavement or main traveled roadway, on a paved road with two or more marked lanes in each direction, or on a one-way street with two or more marked lanes.

Funeral processions and convoys have the right of way at intersections, their vehicles usually use headlamps for identification while the first and last vehicles usually carry distinctive markings, and you should not drive between vehicles in a funeral procession.

Passing is banned within one hundred feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, while a hill or curve requires seven hundred to one thousand feet of clear distance before passing.
When vehicles approach an intersection at the same time, yield to the car on the right, while a driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to pose a hazard.
Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left or when two or more lanes run your way, while passing on the right shoulder is never allowed.

The slow-moving vehicle emblem is an eighteen-inch reflective triangle for vehicles built for twenty-five miles per hour or less, while the no passing zone pennant is a yellow sign on the left side of the road.

After coming to a stop at a red light, you may turn right unless a sign prohibits it, while you may turn left on red from a one-way street into a one-way street where traffic moves to the left unless a sign prohibits that turn.
A red X lane control signal means the lane belongs to opposing traffic, while a red arrow means stop for that lane just as a red light would.
A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, while a right turn on red requires yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles.
A crash must be reported to police at three thousand dollars of property damage, while a bodily-injury lawsuit becomes possible at five thousand dollars of medical bills.
Non-compliance with the safety responsibility law costs the driver's license by suspension, while non-compliance with the insurance law can also cost the vehicle's registration certificate.
The adult threshold for administrative revocation is point zero eight, while the zero tolerance threshold for drivers under twenty-one is point zero two.

A failed test and a refused test both trigger administrative revocation with a thirty-day temporary permit, while refusal adds a one, two or four year revocation based on prior alcohol enforcement contacts.
To check for a safe following gap of at least two seconds, watch the vehicle ahead pass a roadside marker and count one thousand one, one thousand two before reaching that spot.
Hazard flashers warn of a vehicle stopped in a hazardous position and are never used while moving, while turn signals are used for every turn and lane change while moving.

Complete steering failure almost never happens on a well-maintained vehicle, but a partial loss can occur with power steering, in which case you must apply greater effort to the wheel and never give up on steering.
A missed freeway exit means continuing to the next exit, while needing the opposite direction means leaving at the next exit and re-entering, never crossing the divider or turning around.

Before sunrise and after sunset you should turn on low-beam headlamps so others can see you, while if an oncoming vehicle's lights are too bright at night you should flash your high beams once and look toward the right edge of the road.
Motorcyclists are more vulnerable to injury than car drivers in a crash, while over two thirds of crashes between cars and motorcycles happen when a car driver turns in front of the motorcyclist.

When a registered owner's address changes from the one on the registration application, the owner must notify the county agency in writing within thirty days, giving the old and new addresses, the vehicle license number, the make and the vehicle identification number.
A temporary permit runs until the out-of-state registration expires but never beyond twelve months, while a Hawaii registration expires at the end of its own twelfth month every year.

A new vehicle from another state needs a manufacturer's certificate of origin or a notarized bill of sale, while a used vehicle from another state needs the title, the registration and a notarized bill of sale from the named seller.
Yellow warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs.

A rectangular Do Not Pass sign marks locations on two-lane or three-lane roads where passing is forbidden, while a yellow and black pennant-shaped No Passing Zone sign on the left side of the road points to the start of a no-passing zone.

An exclusion sign uses a red circle, with or without a diagonal slash, to prohibit a movement or activity, while other regulatory signs use black or red lettering on white to state restrictions in words.
Guide and information signs in green, blue or brown locate places and services, while warning signs in yellow describe hazards.

A motorist passing a bicyclist should keep at least three feet of clearance until safely past, while opening a vehicle door unexpectedly in a way that creates a hazard for moving traffic or bicyclists is a traffic violation.

A pedestrian must cross only within crosswalks rather than jaywalking, while a pedestrian facing a green light that has been showing for some time should wait for the green signal on the next cycle before starting across.

The inattentive driver drives with one arm out the window, gestures while talking to passengers, pays little attention to traffic, daydreams or gazes off the road when alone, and forfeits safety through that inattention.
Wear the lap and shoulder belt low and snug, place a baby in a car safety seat using an infant seat or a convertible seat in the infant or toddler position, and never carry a baby in your arms.
A baby rides in a car safety seat using an infant seat or a convertible seat in the infant or toddler position, while placing an infant facing forward is listed under ways not to use a seat.
